answer.rationale: The obvious move under competitive price pressure is promotional_pricing, and memory_73 as consolidated ('effective... strong acquisition and revenue lift') would endorse it. But the recovered source, exp_73, shows what that summary dropped: 30-day retention -12% and an explicit instruction not to generalize targeted discounting as sustainable growth. The acquired cohort does not survive first renewal, so discounting would convert a churn problem into a churn-plus-margin problem and would directly contradict the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Matching a competitor's second, deeper cut also invites a race we cannot win. That gap between memory_73 and exp_73 is the important signal for the rest of this decision: consolidated memories here can retain the headline lift and lose the retention cost. memory_31, memory_86, memory_91 and memory_57 are all of the same shape — activation, completion and engagement wins with no retention figure recovered — so I treat them as directionally useful but unproven on durability, not as settled fact. enterprise_sales_assist is the best-verified item (exp_44: retention 0%, qualified revenue +18%) but its own conclusion scopes it to enterprise; it does nothing for the SMB base that is actually churning, though it remains worth running in parallel on its verified enterprise scope. referral_incentive targets established customers, but incentivized referrals from a price-shocked base risk importing the same price-sensitive adverse selection exp_73 exposed. Onboarding changes act on new signups, while the churn conversations are with existing accounts. Activation messaging is the intervention that acts in-product on accounts already present, and the durable defense against a price cut is delivered value rather than matched price. I am running it as a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout precisely because memory_91 evidences week-one engagement and says nothing about renewal, and I will instrument 30/90-day retention and qualified revenue per retained account as primary endpoints — not activation rate, which is the metric class that made exp_73 look like a win. When the archive reopens I want the source records behind memory_91, memory_86, memory_31 and memory_57 to check whether a retention cost was summarized away there too.
